title: Onboarding a tenant only offers beds in the selected property, and calls every space a bed
description: User-reported, two problems on the same screen. FIRST: tapping + on the Tenants tab opens the bed picker, which shows vacant beds in the SELECTED property only. Confirmed in code - BedPickerViewModel reads hostelPreferences.selectedHostelId and walks that hostel's floors alone, so a warden with three properties has to go to the Property tab, switch property, and come back before they can onboard someone into it. Nothing on the picker says it is narrowed, so an empty list reads as 'no space anywhere' when there is space next door. This is the same scoping LODGY-70 removed from the room view and LODGY-81 removed from Home; the picker was missed. SECOND: the picker speaks only in beds. A shop, warehouse or flat IS the unit being let (LODGY-79), and its implicit floor is the placeholder '-', so the picker offers 'Room Corner shop . Bed A' under a floor heading of '-'. BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already handle this - they name the property directly and show the property type where a floor would go - so the vocabulary exists and this screen does not use it. NOTE, NOT IN SCOPE: the transfer screen (TransferViewModel) is hostel-scoped in the same way and has the same bed-only wording. Moving a tenant to a different PROPERTY is a different decision from onboarding, so it is left alone deliberately rather than swept in; the PO should say whether they want it.
acceptanceCriteria: The picker offers every vacant space across all properties, not only the selected one
Each choice says which property it is in, since two properties can both have a Room 101
A shop, warehouse or flat is offered as the whole unit, with no floor, no room number and no bed label
A hostel is unchanged: floor, room and bed, grouped the way it is today
The wording works for a warden who has both kinds of property in one list
The empty and no-properties states say something true now that the list spans everything
Consistent with how BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already name single-unit properties, not a third style
Correct in Hindi as well as English

history.note: Filed from direct user feedback: 'when I click + on tenant screen, I only see beds for the property I had selected. I want to see all beds. Also the term beds does not make sense for flat, warehouse, shop.' Checked against the code before filing; findings recorded in the description.
Starting. Reusing the vocabulary BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already established for single-unit properties rather than inventing a third style, per AC7.

Built. BedPickerViewModel no longer touches hostelPreferences at all - it takes one BedRepository and calls a new DAO query, getVacantChoices(), which returns every vacant bed across every property with its hostel id, hostel name and property type, ordered by property name, floor sortOrder, room number, bed label. Grouping in the ViewModel therefore preserves the SQL order rather than re-sorting. It also replaces the old per-floor, per-room fan-out of flows - the picker used to run one query per floor and one per room, which grew with the property; it is now one query. SHAPE OF THE LIST: property header, then floor headers, then choices. A single-unit property is collapsed to one unlabelled floor in the ViewModel, so the screen never has to decide whether a floor is real - it reads 'The whole property' with the type ('Shop') beneath, and no floor, room number or bed label anywhere on it (AC3). A hostel is unchanged (AC4). This follows the wording BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already use rather than inventing a third style (AC7). EMPTY STATES: 'nothing is vacant in any of your properties' and 'add a property first' are now distinguished by a new hasAnyBed() check, because they need different actions from the warden (AC6). The title changed from 'Pick a Vacant Bed' to 'Where are they moving in?' - it has to be true of a shop and a bed alike, and it reads as a question an older warden can answer (AC5). VERIFIED ON DEVICE with a deliberately mixed portfolio - I freed one space in Corner shop and one in Moonlight so all three properties appeared at once. The list read: 'Corner shop / The whole property / Shop', then 'Moonlight / Ground / Room 501 . Bed A', then 'Sunrise PG' with its floors and 46 beds. Before this change the same screen showed Sunrise PG only. Correct in Hindi: 'वे कहाँ रह रहे हैं?', 'पूरी प्रॉपर्टी', 'दुकान', 'कमरा 501 · बेड A'. The fixture's occupancy has been restored to what it was. NOT DONE, and flagged rather than swept in: the transfer screen is hostel-scoped in the same way and has the same bed-only wording, as recorded in the description. Moving a tenant to a different property is a different decision from onboarding, so it needs the PO rather than me. TESTS: 6 new covering all-properties, hostel floor grouping, single-unit collapsing, a mixed portfolio, and the two empty states. Full suite 541 pass, 0 failures, coverage 95.91% line against the 0.93 gate. Not schema-affecting - the new query and hasAnyBed() read existing columns.

PASS - all eight. The fix is real and I verified it against the failure, not just the success: with a deliberately mixed portfolio the picker listed 'Corner shop / The whole property / Shop', then 'Moonlight / Ground / Room 501 . Bed A', then 'Sunrise PG' with its floors - where before it showed only whichever property happened to be selected (AC1, AC2). AC3 is the one I pushed on: I built a genuinely vacant shop - bed VACANT and its agreement CLOSED, not just a flipped status - and it appeared as 'The whole property' with 'Shop' beneath, with no floor heading, no room number and no bed label anywhere on the row. AC4: hostels keep floor headings and bed labels, unchanged. AC5: both kinds sat in one list and each read correctly. AC6: 'Nothing is vacant in any of your properties' and 'Add a property first' are now separate states, which matters because they need different actions. AC7: this is the same vocabulary BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already use. AC8: correct in Hindi - 'वे कहाँ रह रहे हैं?', 'पूरी प्रॉपर्टी', 'दुकान'. Also noted and correct: a property with nothing vacant does not appear at all, and the per-floor and per-room flow fan-out was replaced by one query. The developer flagged that TransferViewModel is still hostel-scoped with bed-only wording; I agree that is a separate decision and it is not a defect in this ticket.

Accepted. Adding a tenant now shows me every free space across all three properties, so I am not switching property first. My shop is offered as the whole property rather than as a bed inside itself, which is how I think about it.
